newsitem.title: USA: Astros sign deal to stay in Houston.
newsitem.headline: Astros sign deal to stay in Houston.

text.p: The Houston Astros signed an agreement with local officials on Wednesday which they said all but assured the baseball team would stay in the city.

The agreement commits the city of Houston and Harris County to paying up to $180 million for a new downtown stadium while the team and a group of business supporters pay the rest of the expected total cost of $250 million.
"This is the next step in the process, but its a big step...it puts us a long way down the road toward finishing this project," Harris County Judge Robert Eckels said.
Astros' owner Drayton McLane earlier threatened to sell the team if he did not get a new stadium.

Houston voters approved financing for the stadium last November. Proposed tax hikes in the financing package were approved recently by the Texas Legislature, but the final agreement with the Astros was still pending until Wednesday.
It commits the team to staying in Houston for at least 30 years.

Eckels said the last big potential barrier to the deal comes in September when a contract will be signed with a construction contractor. If the contractor wants more than $250 million to build the stadium, the Astros have the right to opt out of the deal, he said.
Officials hope to break ground on the new stadium, which will have a retractable roof, by November and finish it in time for the year 2000 baseball season.
